source: sars-guide:PAYE-GEN-01-G21 Rev 1 p. 11-12 (employer medical contribution is a taxable fringe benefit, deemed paid by the employee: code 3810 added to 4005; medical scheme fees tax credit R376 / R376 / R254)
sourceRef: https://www.sars.gov.za/wp-content/uploads/Ops/Guides/PAYE-GEN-01-G21-Guide-for-Employers-iro-Employees-Tax-for-2027-External-Guide.pdf ; SARS e@syFile Employer Reconciliation BRS (SARS_PAYE_BRS V25.3.0, Jun-26) codes 3810 p. 94, 4474 p. 103
notes: R25 000 salary; the employer pays R3 000 a month to a medical scheme for the employee and one dependant. G21 p. 12: that contribution is a taxable fringe benefit, deemed paid by the employee, so code 3810 (R3 000) is remuneration and the same value counts as deemed contributions (4005) for the medical scheme fees tax credit: R376 + R376 = R752 a month (G21 p. 11, 2027). Taxable 28 000; x12 = 336 000; tax = 44 118 + 26% x (336 000 - 245 100) = 67 752; less 17 820 = 49 932; /12 = 4 161.00; less R752 = 3409.00. The Seventh Schedule para 12A / s6A-6B wording is not fetched (named limit); the G21 p. 11-12 text is the source. The 3810 earning is entered as taxable cash here because the oracle component type cannot carry a non-cash benefit; employer UIF/SDL on it are not asserted. NAMED LIMIT: because 3810 is entered as a cash earning, this case guards the tables and the medical credits only; it passes today and does not exercise FB's non-cash path. FB must add a non-cash 3810 assertion (and the 65+ deemed 4474 credit) when it builds that path. SDL AND NET ADDED (FB review round 2): SDL: 1% x the R25 000 salary = R250.00 (the 3810 is not SDL-flagged here). Net = R25 000 cash (the 3810 is non-cash) - PAYE 3 409.00 - UIF 177.12 = R21413.88; the benefit is non-cash, so it is in neither gross nor net pay. These two figures are derived from the cited rules and the sourced PAYE and UIF, not read from a payslip.
